title: fix: stop emitting a duplicate pcb_cutout for every HOLE record
description: Fixes the issue of duplicate pcb_cutout emissions for each HOLE record in EasyEDA, ensuring that only a single pcb_hole is reported for component mounting holes.
body:
## Summary

Every EasyEDA `HOLE` shape produced **two** circuit elements at identical coordinates:

```ts
circuitElements.push(handleHole(h, index))
circuitElements.push(handleHoleCutout(h, index))
```

`handleHole` emits `pcb_hole`. `handleHoleCutout` emitted a board-level `pcb_cutout` circle at the same center and radius. So a component mounting hole was reported to consumers as both a hole *and* a board cutout.

This contradicts the project's own contract:

- `docs/elements/cutout.mdx` scopes `<cutout>` to board-outline milling.
- `docs/elements/hole.mdx` explicitly sanctions `<hole>` inside a `<footprint />`.
- `docs/footprints/` — the footprint-legal element catalogue — does not list `cutout`.
- `lib/websafe/generate-footprint-tsx.ts:54-55` already documented the redundancy: *"Circular cutouts created alongside HOLE records are already emitted as `<hole>`; polygon board outlines and solid regions need their own element."*

`handleHoleCutout` was added in `09d764c` (PR #247) as scaffolding, not for a separate purpose. It had exactly one caller and no other references. The cutout's real sources (solid-region cutouts, NPTH, and layer-10 board outlines) are untouched.

### Effect on consumers

- `circuit-to-svg` painted each mounting hole twice at the same coordinates. Pre-fix `tests/convert-to-soup-tests/__snapshots__/c5184526.snap.svg` contained a `pcb_cutout` circle and a `pcb_hole` circle with byte-identical `cx`, `cy`, and `r` values, confirming the duplicate paint rather than inferring it.
- A downstream drill exporter that treats board cutouts as drill targets could emit duplicate hits.
- The stray `pcb_cutout` is board-level (no `pcb_component_id`), so a soup consumer sees a *board* cutout for what is a component mounting hole.

## Fix

Delete `handleHoleCutout` and its call site. `handleHole` is unchanged.

```diff
-const handleHoleCutout = (hole: z.infer<typeof HoleSchema>, index: number) => {
-  return Soup.pcb_cutout.parse({
-    type: "pcb_cutout",
-    pcb_cutout_id: `pcb_cutout_from_hole_${index + 1}`,
-    shape: "circle",
-    center: { x: milx10(hole.center.x), y: milx10(hole.center.y) },
-    radius: milx10(hole.radius),
-  } as Soup.PcbCutoutCircleInput)
-}
-
     .forEach((h, index) => {
       circuitElements.push(handleHole(h, index))
-      circuitElements.push(handleHoleCutout(h, index))
     })
```

## Test change

`tests/convert-to-soup-tests/c19795120-cutout.test.ts` asserted `cutouts.length > 0`. C19795120's only cutout source *was* the redundant emission, so that assertion encoded the bug as expected behavior. It now asserts:

```ts
// C19795120 has no board cutout, only a mounting hole. The prior assertion
// encoded the duplicate emission as expected behavior.
expect(cutouts.length).toBe(0)
expect(holes.length).toBe(1)
```

## Snapshot change

One snapshot, purely subtractive:

`tests/convert-to-soup-tests/__snapshots__/c5184526.snap.svg` — two `<circle class="pcb-cutout ...">` elements removed; `pcb_hole` count unchanged at 2.

## Verification

- `tests/convert-to-soup-tests/`: **34 pass, 0 fail**
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `bun run format:check` (CI's exact command): clean, 242 files

## Scope note

Before this change, every EasyEDA HOLE record emitted a redundant `pcb_cutout_from_hole_*` element alongside its `pcb_hole`. Measured across the committed fixture corpus:

```
before: 12 fixtures with a HOLE record, 22 pcb_cutout_from_hole_* elements
after:  12 fixtures with a HOLE record,  0 pcb_cutout_from_hole_* elements
```

Only one golden file changes. The other 11 fixtures never rendered their cutout into SVG, so the duplication was present in circuit-json but not captured by a snapshot. Every duplicate is gone from the JSON; only one golden file happened to paint the affected geometry.

title: Render teardrops for equivalent source traces
description: Fixes the issue where teardrops for equivalent source traces were not rendered correctly, leading to missing teardrops on routed copper.
body:
Routes for one physical net can be attributed to any equivalent source trace. The post-routing teardrop phase matched only the requesting source trace ID, so split traces on the same net silently lost requested teardrops.

The fix follows routed copper through the shared subcircuit connectivity key while retaining the exact-ID fallback. It is stacked on #4621, so the same PCB snapshot naturally changes from the missing taper to the rendered teardrop.

title: Repro: teardrop missing from equivalent source trace
description: Fixes the issue where a requested teardrop is missing when routed copper is attributed to another source trace on the same physical net.
body:
A trace can request a teardrop while its routed copper is attributed to another source trace on the same physical net. Core currently searches by exact source trace ID, so the requested teardrop is missing.

The regression and PCB snapshot record the missing taper. The fix is stacked in #4619.

title: repro: rotated USB-C oval shield slots short CC traces
description: Reproduces a bug where CC traces of a rotated USB-C connector touch grounded shield slots, providing a comprehensive test to validate the issue.
body:
Rotating a USB-C connector by 90° lets both CC traces cross its grounded oval shield slots. The plated holes retain their rotation in Circuit JSON, but the oval branch in `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` omits it when creating routing obstacles.

Adds a self-contained TSX reproduction of a 5 V USB-C power breakout with two 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs, a 1 µF capacitor, and a two-pin output header. The USB4105-compatible connector footprint uses native `<smtpad>`, `<platedhole>`, and `<silkscreenrect>` JSX. Its geometry comes from this [pinned published export](https://github.com/AnasSarkiz/new_tscircuit_landing_page/blob/066cba26d9e773b76cd97baa7538ba7c7a11f74e/public/circuit/tscircuit.json), translated into footprint-local coordinates. Separate contact labels let every VBUS/GND contact be connected. No JSON fixture is needed at runtime.

Default autorouting routes both CC connections with zero placement errors or ambiguous ports, while DRC reports two accidental contacts with the grounded shell slots. The existing labeled PCB snapshot shows both contacts.

Validation of the TSX conversion:
- The repro executes against published `@tscircuit/core@0.0.2151` and `@tscircuit/checks@0.0.253`; the existing snapshot matches, all 18 copper pads and both rotated oval slots remain, and exactly two accidental shield contacts are reported.
- Removing `test.failing` fails only on the intended contact count: expected 0, received 2. Snapshot and contact-count verification also run outside the expected-failure wrapper in the local validation harness.
- Scoped TypeScript checking of the TSX against the published core/props types, Biome, and whitespace checks pass.
- The source-checkout test command is blocked locally by the unavailable unpublished `@tscircuit/flex-utils` dependency. The published-version check uses the same core version as this PR.

Tests-only reproduction and its existing snapshot.

![USB-C power breakout with CC traces touching grounded shield slots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rushabhcodes/core/7cfb9a8cf4167d9fdd03ec64e581610cf40977b2/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-usb-c-rotated-oval-shield-routing-pcb.snap.svg)

body:
## Problem and change

`<solderpaste>` is defined by `@tscircuit/props`, but Core rejects it as an unregistered element. This adds the native primitive so one continuous copper pad can carry several independent stencil apertures.

The renderer uses the existing props and `pcb_solder_paste` schemas, supports rectangles and circles on either outer layer, and preserves parent rotations, footprint flips, layout movement, and removal. Cached subcircuits retain independent apertures and their orientation, including suppressed full-pad openings. User props remain immutable.

Uses the published `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util@0.0.122`, which includes https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/pull/238. Cached PCB primitives use the shared transform utility. Circuit JSON import retains an aperture's existing rotation as derived state because authored solder-paste props only expose axis-aligned shapes.

Cached circular through-hole paste is restored as independent paste geometry, so inflated round holes must not generate it again. This uses Core's existing `_isInflatedFromCircuitJson` state. Two focused regressions verify that a mixed footprint keeps three automatic paste records and that an explicitly overlapping aperture is preserved, with caching on and off. Each new regression has its own file and labeled snapshot. Pill and oval generation are unchanged.

Includes ten solder-paste tests, including a six-window pattern over a single exposed copper pad. Updated to main's `isSmt` support; keeps `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.701` and the released paste transformation fix.

Fixes #3577.

## Validation

- All 10 solder-paste tests pass. The two new cache regressions failed before the fix (5 instead of 3 records, and 6 instead of 4).
- Focused suite: 34 pass, 1 existing pill-paste snapshot mismatch. The 0.12% mismatch reproduces on unchanged main `f518678` with the same dependencies and produces an identical diff image; its snapshot is unchanged.
- Existing `isSmt` tests, manual-via regression, and standalone primitive caching pass. The manual-via test now matches main exactly.
- Polygon plated-hole test and both new snapshot comparisons pass after removing ternaries from the newly touched primitive.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, and `bun run smoke-test:dist` pass.
- `bun run format`, `git diff --check`, and `INPUT_PACKAGE_TYPE=internal_lib bunx @tscircuit/dependency-check` pass. Zero ternaries in the 17 changed TS/TSX files.
- The neighboring polygon-paste caching snapshot previously showed a 0.04% mismatch on both this PR and unchanged code with the same dependencies. That baseline is unchanged.

The full test suite was not rerun for this update.

## Scope

This implements Core rendering and Circuit JSON import/cache support. It does not change downstream Gerber or KiCad exporters; they must consume independent `pcb_solder_paste` records to preserve these apertures.

title: fix: report disallowed blind/buried vias in manual paths
description: Reports disallowed blind or buried vias in manual paths when the board disables them, preserving saved copper and aggregating all disallowed vias.
body:
Manual `pcbPath` and `pcbPaths` can request blind or buried vias while the board disables them. Report one nonfatal `pcb_trace_error` per affected path, preserving saved copper and aggregating all disallowed vias. Fixes #4526.

The diagnostic starts with `blind vias aren't allowed by allowBlindAndBuriedVias settings in pcbPath` (using `buried` or `blind and buried` for those via kinds, and `pcbPaths[index]` for multiple paths). It identifies the readable trace or connection name, zero-based indices in the original TSX array, resolved layer spans, and board positions, with its marker at the first disallowed via.

The message gives two remedies: use top-to-bottom through vias with matching adjoining wire layers, or set `allowBlindAndBuriedVias={true}` on `<board>` when fabrication supports blind/buried vias. The visual regression displays the actual diagnostic opening, including the setting name, in both its heading and callouts. The disconnected manual-via regression verifies both renderer and final DRC contact errors.

Validation for the latest follow-up (Bun 1.4.0):
- Four focused regression tests pass, including both changed tests and their visual snapshots, without update mode.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, Biome formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The separate `trace-multiple-pcb-paths` snapshot has a local 0.25% font difference that also reproduces with the unmodified PR code; its geometry and assertions pass.

title: Resolve named traces and diagnose invalid routing-phase selectors
description: Fixes autorouting failure by resolving bare trace names and explicit trace selectors, ensuring proper diagnostics for unmatched or ambiguous selectors.
body:
Autorouting phases now resolve bare trace names such as DDR_D0 and explicit trace selectors such as trace.DDR_D0, alongside existing endpoint selectors. Previously a name-only list selected nothing and silently changed routing order.

Resolve all phase lists before assigning ownership, deduplicate trace objects, and report unmatched or ambiguous selectors with the phase name and actionable examples. Resolution is scoped to the current subcircuit. Breakout-owned traces remain owned by their breakout; rerouting and saved paths retain their behavior. Typed endpoint selectors such as .U1 > port.DQ0 are preserved during identity lookup.

Compatibility: previously ignored invalid selectors now throw before routing. The connection field inside a saved pcbTracePaths entry still selects a port.

Validation: 33 tests passed across 32 files (new selection/diagnostic/scope tests plus existing autoroutingphase coverage); TypeScript --noEmit passed. The name-only regression fails against the original implementation and passes after this change. New PCB snapshots cover the named-selection and sibling-subcircuit cases.

title: Support physical BGA ball names through port resolution and rendering
description: Allows chips and connectors to use physical BGA ball names directly in pinLabels, connections, footprint hints, schematic arrangements, and pin styles, resolving previous issues with alias resolution.
body:
Chips and connectors can now use physical BGA ball names directly in pinLabels, connections, footprint hints, schematic arrangements and pin styles. Previously the schema accepted A1 but component construction and downstream alias resolution rejected it.

Resolve an explicit package map with deterministic row/column ordering, reserving existing numeric pins. Preserve each physical name separately from its schematic ordinal, independently of object and footprint ordering. Physical source ports serialize the ball name and omit a numeric package pin number; their numeric layout ordinal remains on schematic_port through source_port_id. Numeric-key callers retain their existing behavior.

Shared labels such as GND no longer implicitly join distinct physical balls. Connect those balls explicitly to a net; singular ambiguous alias selectors report the physical choices. Pad matching prioritizes physical hints over shared labels or footprint-local numeric hints. Input props are not mutated.

Validation: 28 tests passed across 23 files, including existing pin-label and internal-connection regressions; TypeScript --noEmit passed. New tests cover reordered package/footprint maps, source/schematic/PCB identity and geometry, explicit GND connectivity, ambiguity, unknown balls, mixed numeric pins, and multi-letter rows. PCB and schematic snapshots are included. The new end-to-end physical-ball regression fails against the original core implementation.

KiCad export requires the companion https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/pull/634, which preserves these identities in PCB pads, library pins and placed symbol pins. Its 8 tests and typecheck pass, including numeric-pad compatibility. Older exporter versions do not provide this guarantee; coordinate the releases.

title: Respect component isSmt when generating solder paste
description: Modifies solder paste generation logic to respect the isSmt property, preventing unwanted paste for through-hole components while retaining paste for mixed footprints.
body:
Components with only through-hole pins currently receive automatic solder-paste apertures. This implements the `isSmt` API from https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/932 so through-hole parts can be soldered separately without adding unwanted stencil openings, while mixed footprints such as USB-C keep their existing paste.

| Component | Paste behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `isSmt` omitted, only plated holes | Omit automatic paste |
| `isSmt` omitted, at least one SMT pad | Keep existing paste generation, including plated slots |
| `isSmt={false}` | Omit automatic paste on both SMT pads and plated holes |
| `isSmt={true}` | Keep existing paste generation, including plated-hole-only footprints |

Inference is scoped to the owning component and uses its footprint children, so it does not depend on whether a pad has rendered yet or whether another component on the board is SMT. Copper, drills, paste dimensions, and existing solder-mask/paste-margin rules are unchanged.

The tests cover both explicit values, omitted values, a plated slot appearing before its SMT pad, and a `usbcmidmount` connector beside a through-hole `pinrow2` header. Paste-only snapshots make the openings visible. Existing tests that intentionally exercise through-hole paste now opt in with `isSmt`.

Validation:
- GitHub CI passes: all ten test jobs, typecheck, formatting, and smoke test.
- Local build and TypeScript checking pass.
- All three regression tests fail on the unchanged core implementation and pass with this fix (25 assertions).
- Local snapshot mismatches also reproduce on baseline; rerunning the broader failures with a 30-second timeout gives the same 9 passes and 34 failures on both revisions. The two existing paste snapshots also fail identically on baseline and remain unchanged.

title: fix: align NEMA23 body and curved rear cap
description: Aligns the NEMA23 motor body with a newly designed curved rear cap, ensuring a flush fit without side overhang, while maintaining existing front features and improving rear mounting options.
body:
The default NEMA23 rear repeats the front flange's nearly square outline and square fastener pattern. Render a curved rear cap with side tabs, R5 concave recesses, R2.5 convex fillets, and a 50 × 32 mm rectangular fastener pattern. The body follows the same curved outline, so the rear shoulders stay flush without extra side overhang. The front flange, mounting holes, pilot, shaft, and overall body envelope remain unchanged.

Consumes https://github.com/tscircuit/modelprinter/pull/119

Both rear bores and installed screws use the contract's independent X/Y spacing. Plain caps, blind bores with solid floors, and installed screws share the same rear outline in React and the built vanilla/Node entrypoints. The stepped-profile renderer consumes separate concave/convex radii for the body and rear, including zero-radius corners. Other frame defaults retain their current shapes.

The profile is representative, based on [STEPPERONLINE's ST-M10 rear-adapter drawing](https://www.omc-stepperonline.com/image/catalog/dimensions/ST-M10_Dimension.svg). The motor retains its 56.4 mm envelope and uses illustrative M3 socket screws. The adapter does not establish exact motor threads, screw style, or rear-cover radii; these defaults are not universal NEMA23 dimensions. Matching the body and rear shoulders follows the motor-photo reference. The former depiction remains available with `nema23_chamfered_backholespacing47.14mm_backscrewm4`.

Geometry probes verify the body supports the rear shoulders in all quadrants, along with concave recesses, convex fillets, independent body radii, rectangular bore overrides, blind floors, and unchanged front mounting holes. Standard four-view snapshots cover plain, holes, and screws, labeled with their full model strings.

Validation with `MODELPRINTER_PR=119` and Bun 1.4.3:
- All 22 targeted NEMA geometry, React/vanilla/Node, and visual tests passed.
- Type checking, formatting, and package build passed.
- All 307 tests and required checks passed in the paired parameter-contract repository.

The model gallery consumes these shared libraries and picks up released updates through its existing library-update workflow.

title: Avoid redundant physical connectivity geometry during continuity checks
description: Reduces unnecessary computation in continuity validation by deferring the construction of the physical trace graph until needed, optimizing the process of checking connectivity between traces.
body:
Continuity validation eagerly built the full physical trace graph and every wire capsule, even when endpoint pads already proved the required connection. Defer that graph until needed, index individual wire segments before exact connectivity tests, and construct wire polygons only for nearby barrel/pour contact candidates.

Retain the exact connectivity/contact predicates, layer/width handling, physical via/pour rules, and stable connection ordering. Two regressions cover folded traces and lazy wire contacts at rounded ends, incoming widths, layers and contact boundaries.

Validation:
- Fresh local full suite: 662 tests, 16 snapshots, 8,007 assertions; zero failures. Build and declarations pass.
- All source CI checks pass, including TypeScript, build, format, dependency policy and packed-package consumer.
- SRJ18 sample 2 replay preserves the full net map, per-trace queries, ordered 2,486 physical via/pour edges, continuity errors, and exact final routes (506 vias).
- [Independent autorouter benchmark PR #3063](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3063) runs the immutable package preview against main with #2998 already merged. [Exact `/benchmark --dataset 18` results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3063#issuecomment-6155234232): median -3.7%, P95 -7.0%, total solve time -4.6% (1478.4s → 1410.3s). title: fix: honor GLB accessor stride and normalization
description: Fixes GLB import issues by correctly decoding interleaved vertex data and applying glTF normalization for various component types, ensuring accurate rendering of positions and normals.
body:
Stacked on #257, which captures the broken accessor behavior in PoppyGL. Merge #257 first, then retarget this PR to main.

GLB imports currently read interleaved vertex data as tightly packed components and leave normalized integers at their raw magnitude. This scrambles positions and normals and makes normalized SHORT positions up to 32767× too large.

The PoppyGL snapshot now shows the frozen broken model beside the corrected live render, with identical inputs, PCB placement and camera. Packed FLOAT is unchanged; the interleaved sheet and oversized quantized wall become 1 mm cubes. The repro's exported-dimension assertions now require 1 mm on every axis in all three encodings.

Adds 21 accessor regression cases. Against the original decoder, 17 fail; all pass with this change. The corrected visual snapshot also fails when the original decoder is restored.

body:
Adds `SwitchRcNetworkGroupingSolver`, reporting `SwitchRcNetworkNotGrouped` when a grounded switch, its parallel capacitor, or its local pull resistor is separated from the group. It checks both switch–capacitor spacing and the pull resistor's distance from the nearer member of that pair. A distant resistor is reported even when the switch and capacitor are already together.

The complete controls sheet from [AnasSarkiz/Game-Boy-Enhance v1.0.3](https://tscircuit.com/AnasSarkiz/Game-Boy-Enhance?version=1.0.3#schematic) supplies ten real networks: SW3–SW12, C45–C54, and R26–R35. Stacked on the TSX-only repro #270. The analyzer reports placement advice; the TSX fixture demonstrates the correction.

| Complete 30-component controls sheet | Existing findings | New grouping findings |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original published placement | 10 | 10 |
| Only rotate the capacitors as previously advised | 0 | 10 |
| Group and rotate all ten switch/resistor/capacitor networks | 0 | 0 |
| Regression variant: corrected layout with only R26 moved away | 0 | 1 |

The last row is a deliberate TSX regression variant, not the published placement. Its test verifies that moving only R26 back clears the finding, with every electrical record unchanged.

### Reference and original rendering

[TI SCEA094, page 1](https://www.ti.com/lit/ab/scea094/scea094.pdf#page=1) draws the switch and capacitor as adjacent parallel branches with a pull resistor above their shared signal. Its buffer is not part of this board's controls sheet; the example supports the drawing convention, not a debounce-function inference or a numeric spacing requirement.

| Published TI reference | Original tscircuit controls sheet |
| --- | --- |
| ![TI switch RC network](https://www.ti.com/ods/images/SCEA094/GUID-D22D0495-3892-4401-908A-5C89503658D6-low.gif) | ![Original complete controls sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/d19716adbff5a596c984788fe731b012b74e9454/tests/cases/__snapshots__/gameboy-switch-capacitor-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg) |

### Correction

Single-network detail, at equal scale with a divider. The switch, capacitor, and resistor share one numbered finding:

![SW3 C45 R26 before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/9bf448fbfa268d04ea013c8ffbcbbbd9e234615a/tests/cases/__snapshots__/gameboy-switch-capacitor-pair-comparison.snap.svg)

All ten networks together, with matching numbered diagnostics:

![Complete controls before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/9bf448fbfa268d04ea013c8ffbcbbbd9e234615a/tests/cases/__snapshots__/gameboy-switch-capacitor-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

[Complete corrected sheet at readable scale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/9bf448fbfa268d04ea013c8ffbcbbbd9e234615a/tests/cases/__snapshots__/gameboy-switch-capacitor-correction-full-sheet.snap.svg) · [Full original with the new findings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/9bf448fbfa268d04ea013c8ffbcbbbd9e234615a/tests/cases/__snapshots__/gameboy-switch-capacitor-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg)

The correction retains all 30 components and their symbol definitions, moves/rotates the networks, and reduces the section heading's font size to avoid crowding the supply label. Full placement analysis reports **zero findings on the entire controls sheet**; this does not refer to the other five board sheets.

### Detection and checks

- Uses typed switch/capacitor/resistor records, connectivity, explicit ground/power flags, and schematic scope. No name, pin-label, net-label, or `port_hints` matching establishes a role.
- Requires one grounded two-terminal switch and one capacitor across the same two nets. When present, one local resistor from their signal to an explicitly identified supply joins the group and has its spacing checked. The switch/capacitor check also works without a pull resistor.
- Measures body gaps: switch to capacitor, then resistor to the nearer switch/capacitor. Reports separation beyond the larger of 4 schematic units or twice the larger symbol dimension for the measured pair. This readability heuristic permits staggered placements and label space; it does not demand exact coordinates.
- Skips competing switches/capacitors or pull resistors, a same-sheet signal consumer, unsupported or missing placements/ports, DNP/DNC parts, separate scopes, and intervening unrelated bodies. Off-sheet signal consumers are allowed.
- Guard tests cover both drawing axes, a resistor close to either member, a separated resistor, and ambiguous or obstructed cases. The R26-only regression verifies a single finding before and zero full-sheet findings after moving R26.
- Original-to-corrected tests compare all 163 electrical records. Core's rotation-dependent removal of `pos`/`neg` aliases on the 20 capacitor ports is explicitly checked; all other source fields match. Wire-graph checks verify continuous signal and ground connections on every corrected network.

Validation: **225 tests pass**, typecheck and formatting checks pass, and all four snapshots were rendered and inspected. No dependency changes or unrelated snapshot updates. description: Stacked on 248, the complete TSX repro from pmdroidkey-pcb v1.0.4. Adds SwitchMatrixDiodePlacementSolver to identify two placement problems: 1. A matrix diode is far from its connected switch. 2. Connected matrix rows or columns have excessive unused space after their switchdiode pairs are nearby. The corrected layout uses a compact 34 matrix, reducing the row pitch from 9 to 4 schematic units. All twelve switchdiode connections are drawn as continuous straight wires. Full-sheet placement analysis reports 0 findings with every analyzer enabled; tests verify that electrical source records and pin connections remain unchanged.
body:
Stacked on #248, the complete TSX repro from [pmdroid/key-pcb v1.0.4](https://tscircuit.com/pmdroid/key-pcb?version=1.0.4#schematic).

Adds `SwitchMatrixDiodePlacementSolver` to identify two placement problems:

| Finding | What it detects | Repro result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SwitchMatrixDiodeSeparatedFromSwitch` | A matrix diode is far from its connected switch. | 12 findings on the original sheet; 0 after placing each diode beside its switch. |
| `SwitchMatrixBranchesTooSpreadOut` | Connected matrix rows or columns have excessive unused space after their switch/diode pairs are nearby. | 1 finding on the variant with adjacent pairs but widely spaced rows; 0 after compacting the matrix. |

The corrected layout uses a compact 3×4 matrix, reducing the row pitch from 9 to 4 schematic units. All twelve switch/diode connections are drawn as continuous straight wires. Full-sheet placement analysis reports **0 findings with every analyzer enabled**; tests verify that electrical source records and pin connections remain unchanged.

The complete matrix comparison shows all twelve pairs together. Every before/after image—including the spacing comparison and single-pair close-up—has a gray vertical divider, equal-scale panels, and diagnostics underneath.

![Complete matrix: original left, corrected right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/a710349c8ad02d0b0d12a9437406a6df011ce63b/tests/cases/__snapshots__/switch-matrix-diode-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The spacing comparison isolates the second finding: both versions already have adjacent switch/diode pairs, but only the left has excessive space between rows.

![Matrix spacing: one finding before, zero after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/a710349c8ad02d0b0d12a9437406a6df011ce63b/tests/cases/__snapshots__/switch-matrix-branch-spacing.snap.svg)

Additional committed snapshots:

- [Single SW1/D1 before/after close-up](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/a710349c8ad02d0b0d12a9437406a6df011ce63b/tests/cases/__snapshots__/switch-matrix-diode-pair-comparison.snap.svg), with the same divider and a matching numbered diagnostic.
- [Complete original sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/a710349c8ad02d0b0d12a9437406a6df011ce63b/tests/cases/__snapshots__/keyboard-switch-series-diode-repro-full-sheet.snap.svg): original placements, 12 switch/diode findings and 17 existing findings.
- [Complete corrected sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/a710349c8ad02d0b0d12a9437406a6df011ce63b/tests/cases/__snapshots__/switch-matrix-diode-correction-full-sheet.snap.svg): all 92 components in three broad sections stacked vertically—power/USB/encoder, regulator/microcontroller, and matrix/RGB/test points. A short footer gives the full-sheet issue total. There is no all-analyzer-counts table.

To resolve the 17 existing findings, the corrected TSX also adjusts chip-label clearance, resistor orientations, long branches, the LED4/R_LED label collision, and capacitor grouping. **C_LED1–C_LED12 and C_LS are moved into the VBUS capacitor bank at the bottom of section 1 in the corrected full-sheet snapshot.** They remain connected and present; their new positions are outside the matrix comparison crop. RGB symbols retain their original geometry and are placed below the matrix. The original RGB renderer's missing-port messages remain; the zero count refers to placement-analysis findings.

The original TSX layout and PCB placement are unchanged. The full-sheet sections are crops of one complete render, so wires may continue outside a section boundary. No analyzer is disabled or modified to waive the existing findings.

Detection uses typed two-terminal switches/diodes and connectivity through a private pair connection and both shared buses. Names, pin hints and net labels are not used to infer electrical roles. Ambiguous, isolated, rail-connected, unpopulated and cross-scope branches are skipped.

The spacing check runs within the same solver and reports one finding per connected matrix. It requires a complete rectangular topology and distinct spatial bus bands. It reserves component bodies, ports, labels and schematic text—including intervening circuitry—with 0.5 units of clearance, then checks the largest remaining empty band against `max(4, 3 × largest symbol dimension along that axis)`. This is a schematic readability heuristic, not an electrical limit or a demand for exact alignment. Incomplete matrices and layouts without distinct bus bands are skipped; affected traces must be rerouted after movement.

[TI TIDA-01237, Figure 13 on page 17](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/tiduc45/tiduc45.pdf#page=17) provides the published switch/diode layout reference. Its diode arrays and circuit differ from this keyboard, and it does not prescribe the solver's distance thresholds.

![Published TI reference on the left; original tscircuit rendering on the right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/be24f4dfc96578b980be287cd31467e05afb7e0c/reference-comparison.png)

Validation: **219 tests passed locally**. GitHub's Bun tests, typecheck and formatting all pass on `a710349`. Tests cover preserved electrical records and symbols, all twelve straight pair connections, spacing detection, compact and rotated layouts, separate matrices, intervening components/text/labels, larger symbols, and topology/rail/scope guards. The comparisons and corrected full-sheet sections were visually inspected. No dependency or timeout changes are included.

title: Add ti generate-sysconfig-site for standalone read-only viewing
description: Add ti generate-sysconfig-site file to generate a self-contained, read-only HTML page from .syscfg, Circuit JSON, or TSTSX without requiring TI software or SDK installation.
body:
Add `ti generate-sysconfig-site <file>` to generate a self-contained, read-only HTML page from `.syscfg`, Circuit JSON, or TS/TSX. It requires Bun and the authorised private `@tscircuit/sysconfig-viewer` installed in the input project. It does not discover or run TI SysConfig, CCS, or an installed SDK.

The public TI package contains only the command and orchestration helpers; copied TI interface assets remain in the private viewer package. Existing `.syscfg` is preserved. Circuit inputs use the existing converter; TSX gets a normal PCB-enabled build, and build/conversion errors propagate without suppressing checks. Output is written exclusively to a new file. Missing/incompatible private packages, metadata mismatch and malformed source fail clearly. `--catalog` selects explicit versioned JSON metadata; otherwise the private viewer matches its bundled catalog exactly.

The page displays source choices with SDK declarations/defaults separately. Generation is not TI validation, pin solving or firmware generation. No C outputs, success Problems state or dependency instances are fabricated. This command does not modify CLI/RunFrame tabs, start a server, or deploy a site; Seve owns that integration separately.

Development dependency pins are aligned to the tested tscircuit 0.0.2857 / props 0.0.700 / circuit-json 0.0.528 set, resolving the schema export mismatch encountered with the old dev toolchain. No overrides, type escapes or weakened checks.

Viewer PRs #6 and #7 are now both on main through merged PR #8. The setup documentation pins the actual resulting main commit `527364cac16ae00204f875c5a57704f195f96992` and explains how to pack and install that private package in the circuit project. No private Git dependency or vendor assets are added to the public TI distribution.

The resulting main commit has exactly the same tracked file tree (`1e99586b5bc8544ca48da803ad3367603588b378`) as the previously tested merged URL-viewer revision `d7ff1bd564f9a256a2ab9c434a1e8656b8965bf3`. This update only changes the documentation pin and removes stale feature-branch instructions. No local tests or builds were rerun for this pin-only update, as requested.

Prior validation of the unchanged implementation:
- 65 Node CLI tests and 3 Bun CLI tests pass, including the site-command protocol tests and existing inline snapshots.
- Typecheck, formatting, npm build, and isolated local/global npm consumer checks pass.
- Fresh consumer projects using archives of both actual merged viewer trees successfully generated real standalone HTML from the configured imrishabh18/pedometer `.syscfg` and Circuit JSON. Embedded source exactly matches the original/converter output, with SHA256 `9d4e48a9d6a4c0c65216ab54d4b83e1c09459ea8fb4653cbc6d5937f43c3f3b6`.
- Missing QFP dimensions, out-of-range physical pins and an explicit RTOS/catalog mismatch are rejected before HTML is written. Original source and existing outputs are preserved.
- These real-viewer runs used no TI installation or renderer mock. Separate subprocess fixtures cover the protocol only and are not UI parity evidence.

A normal TSX build of the physical pedometer currently reports board DRC issues; they are separate from this source-viewer command and are not bypassed. The end-to-end checks above start from its existing Circuit JSON/`.syscfg`. The viewer is read-only and does not claim complete TI application parity.

The tscircuit registry build failure is the known infrastructure status and is not treated as a blocker for this update, as requested. No TI merge, release or deployment.

title: fix: align NEMA23 body and curved rear cap with rectangular rear pattern
description: Aligns the NEMA23 rear cap with a new curved design and rectangular rear pattern, ensuring proper fit and validation against existing dimensions.
body:
The NEMA23 rear previously reused the front flange's nearly square outline and square fastener pattern. Define a curved rear cap with a 50 × 32 mm rectangular rear pattern, R5 concave recesses, and R2.5 outer fillets. The default body now follows that same curved outline, so the rear shoulders do not protrude beyond an octagonal body. The front flange, mounting holes, pilot, shaft, and body envelope remain unchanged.

Paired renderer: https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/503

Add independent rear X/Y spacing, rear profile selectors, and configurable body/rear arc radii. Existing scalar rear spacing still sets both axes. Keep the former body and rear depiction available with `nema23_chamfered_backholespacing47.14mm_backscrewm4`. Other frame defaults retain their current shapes.

Validate rear bores and screw heads against the actual straight edges and curved shoulders, and validate the entire front through-hole radius against the body profile. Wire references follow the selected outline. The shared analytic checks do not introduce renderer dependencies.

The rear profile and pattern use [STEPPERONLINE's ST-M10 rear-adapter drawing](https://www.omc-stepperonline.com/image/catalog/dimensions/ST-M10_Dimension.svg) as a representative reference. The motor retains its 56.4 mm envelope and uses illustrative M3 socket screws. Matching body/rear shoulders follows the motor-photo reference.

title: Support the RP2040 DRV8825 and RGB controller board

Voltage changes disable the driver and enforce a settling interval; temperature, heartbeat, watchdog and driver-fault protection remain active. With the replacement charger and an explicit 9 V request, two 800-microstep forwardreverse moves completed with exact commanded counts, about 0.87 A peak absolute winding samples and no reported faults; the user confirmed the motor spun. title: feat: add noSolderPaste to all SMT pad shapes
description: Adds noSolderPaste?: boolean to the TypeScript interfaces and Zod schemas for every smtpad shape: rect, rotated rect, circle, pill, rotated pill, and polygon, allowing TSX authors to express testprobe pads with exposed copper and no solder paste.
body:
Adds `noSolderPaste?: boolean` to the TypeScript interfaces and Zod schemas for every `<smtpad>` shape: rect, rotated rect, circle, pill, rotated pill, and polygon. This lets TSX authors express test/probe pads with exposed copper and no solder paste, including pads inside footprints.

Related to https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/4630.

The parser accepts only booleans, preserves explicit `true`/`false`, and leaves omitted values undefined. The intended behavior is that `true` suppresses paste independently of solder mask settings and takes precedence over `solderPasteMargin`; omission or `false` preserves existing paste behavior. There are no aliases or migration requirements. Core still needs to consume this prop to suppress `pcb_solder_paste` generation.

Includes tests for all six shapes, omitted and explicit values, coexistence with mask and margin settings, and invalid inputs. Regenerated all required documentation.

Validation: `bun test` (680 passed), `tsc --noEmit`, `biome format .`, and `bun run build` passed.

title: fix: parse explicit polarity pins in diode footprint strings
description: Fixes the parsing of explicit polarity pins in diode footprint strings to ensure correct polarity markings without altering copper pad numbers or retaining supplier artwork.
body:
Explicit polarity modifiers such as `diode_p3.4mm_pw1.2mm_ph0.95mm_rounded0_cathodepin1` throw `Diode cathode pin must be 1 or 2`, although the equivalent numeric builder call works. Footprinter strings pass numeric modifier values as strings; the generic diode generator forwarded them to the fabrication-note helper without normalizing them.

Parse the common options through the existing schema before passing the anode/cathode pins to the helper. This generates the correct polarity markings without changing copper pad numbers or retaining supplier artwork.

The regression covers both modifier names on either physical pin, compares string output with the builder, rejects conflicting polarity assignments, and includes one PCB SVG snapshot.

Validation:
- Confirmed the new regression fails before the change.
- `bun test tests/diode.test.ts tests/diode-fabrication-notes.test.ts tests/sod123w.test.ts` — 41 passed.
- `bun run build` — JavaScript and declarations passed.
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Required by the revised diode-identity solution in tscircuit/cli#5371.

title: fix: translate rounded board outlines to the resolved board center
description: Fixes alignment of generated rounded board outlines with the resolved board center during rendering, preventing false outside-board errors.

Translate generated rounded board outlines to the resolved board center during initial rendering and auto-sizing. This keeps the outline aligned with `pcbX`/`pcbY` and prevents false outside-board errors.

title: fix: avoid extra built-in terminals when custom symbols declare ports
description: Fixes the issue of extra built-in terminals being created when a custom symbol declares its own ports, preventing false unconnected-pin warnings.
body:
SW4’s custom symbol declares six ports: `1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7`. Core also adds pin4 from the built-in DPDT symbol, causing a false unconnected-pin warning.

This fix prevents extra built-in terminals from being created when a custom symbol declares its own ports. Existing port matching and positioning stay intact. Custom drawings without ports keep the default fallback, and partial `pinLabels` still work.

TSX tests and SVG snapshots cover SW4, drawings without ports, partial pin labels, and genuine unconnected-pin warnings. **12 switch tests and type-checking passed.**

Stacked on the reproduction PR #4644.

title: repro: custom DPDT symbol gains a phantom pin4
description: Fixes the issue where the custom DPDT symbol incorrectly inherits an extra phantom pin4, leading to missing trace warnings.
body:
SW4 (`JS202011JCQN`) has pins **1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7**, but core adds **pin4** from the built-in DPDT symbol and reports `Port pin4 on SW4 is missing a trace`.

The test inlines the project's **exact schematic symbol and pinLabels** from `pico-pd-motor-lab/imports/JS202011JCQN.tsx`: all six ports, original coordinates and stem lengths, seven paths, contact-link markings, reference text and “DPDT • shown OFF” legend are unchanged. An AST comparison against the project verified equality, ignoring formatting.

The test uses the original SW4 wiring from `circuit/power-switch.tsx`: pin1/pin5 to GND, pin2 to POWER_SWITCH_EN, pin3 to POWER_ON_LEVEL, pin6 to ARM_BASE, and only pin7 marked no-connect. The symbol is defined directly in `tests/repros/repro-custom-dpdt-phantom-pin.test.tsx`; there is no separate symbol fixture file. PCB/CAD assets are omitted because this is a schematic/source-port regression.

The native SVG shows the exact symbol, its original net connections, the actual emitted source-pin list and the checker message. Explanatory notes are outside the symbol. The test deliberately asserts the current broken behavior; no production code is changed.

![Exact SW4 symbol: six real terminals but seven generated source ports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/f3d37d1a9bc64c2c4742ce03d02ebecf1b208fd0/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-custom-dpdt-phantom-pin-schematic.snap.svg)

Validation:

- Exact symbol and pinLabels match the project in an AST comparison.
- Repro and existing switch/no-connect tests: 7 passed.
- `bunx --no-install tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- Biome formatting and visual inspection of the generated SVG: passed.

The fix is stacked on this reproduction in #4645.

title: Prefer exact PCB-port route endpoints
description: Prefers exact PCB-port matches for routed endpoints to avoid incorrect source trace attribution when endpoints fall inside adjacent pads.
body: A routed endpoint can land exactly on a PCB port while also falling inside an adjacent pad. Geometry-based attribution collected both candidates and could select the wrong source trace. This prefers exact PCB-port matches before pad containment. The stacked #4632 snapshot naturally removes the connectivity DRC.

title: Repro adjacent-pad trace attribution DRC

body: Adds a reduced LMG342X repro where a routed endpoint lands exactly on the FB PCB port while also overlapping the adjacent VOUT pad. The current geometry lookup attributes the route to VOUT, and the PCB snapshot shows the resulting connectivity DRC.

title: fix: honor oval plated-hole rotation during autorouting
description: Fixes autorouting issues by ensuring that oval plated-hole dimensions are correctly rotated and used as routing obstacles during PCB design.
body: A USB-C connector rotated by 90° has correctly rotated oval shield-slot copper, but routing obstacles use its unrotated dimensions. In the merged TSX repro (#4618), both CC traces touch the grounded shield slots. Normalize oval plated-hole outer bounds with the existing quarter-turn rectangle helper: a 2.2 × 3.2 mm slot becomes a 3.2 × 2.2 mm obstacle at 90°/270°. Other angles retain their CCW rotation. Activate the merged repro and update its PCB snapshot; the fixed board routes both CC connections with zero DRC errors. Add a TSX regression and labeled snapshot covering 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°, and 33° on both board sides. Expected quarter-turn bounds come from transformed corners of the emitted hole geometry. Validation: - The edited source converter, wired into the matching published core 0.0.2152 renderer/router, passes the USB-C repro, the new rotation test, and the existing rotated-rectangle routing test. - The unfixed pipeline fails only on the USB-C contact assertion: expected zero contacts, received two. The fixed pipeline produces zero board DRC errors. - Three native source obstacle tests pass: identity preservation, circular via obstacles, and ten-layer drilled obstacles. - Scoped TypeScript checks for the changed converter and TSX tests, Biome 1.9.4, and whitespace checks pass. Full source-checkout tests are blocked locally by the unavailable unpublished `@tscircuit/flex-utils` dependency. The functional validation uses the actual edited source converter with the matching published renderer/router; its harness remains outside the repository.

title: Fix footprint keepouts staying behind after PCB layout
description: Fixes the issue where footprint keepouts do not move with their associated PCB components during layout, allowing copper to intrude into designated clearance areas.
body: PCB grid placement moves a module's pads and notes while leaving its footprint keepout at its initial position, allowing copper into the intended antenna clearance. Emit the owning `pcb_component_id` and actual enclosing `pcb_group_id` for rectangle and circle keepouts so the existing layout utilities move them with their owner. Inside ``, `pcbY={15.8}` is a footprint-local offset, not a fixed board position. The keepout and green note rectangle start with that same offset and should receive the chip's layout translation. Previously the keepout lacked ownership, so layout moved the note rectangle but left the keepout behind. Reuse the existing repro from #4522 and update its existing snapshot. Remove the unrelated pinheader and extra antenna decorations; two grid columns still force the single chip to move. With the original code, the keepout stays at `(0, 15.8)` while the marker moves to `(-26.6, 0.9)`; this fix aligns them. No new tests or dependency changes. Validation: - [GitHub Actions test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/38519476466) passes all 10 test jobs. - CI typecheck, distribution smoke tests, package preview, formatting, and dependency checks pass. - 30 existing keepout, copper-pour, grid, flex, and manual-via tests pass locally. - The simplified keepout regression fails at its position assertion when the original keepout emission is restored. - Biome and `git diff --check` pass. Local tests used an isolated dependency install with published Circuit JSON 0.0.525 and Git sources for dependencies whose archive downloads are blocked in this environment.

title: fix: respect rotated pad geometry when assigning routed source traces
description: Fixes incorrect source trace assignments for routed traces on rotated SMT pads, resolving trace-continuity validation failures.
body: Rotated SMT pads were matched using their unrotated dimensions, so routed INA237 SDA and SCL traces inherited adjacent pins’ source metadata even though their copper reached the correct pads. This fixes the bug reproduced in #4527, which also caused trace-continuity validation failures on the full INA237 board. Endpoints and pad centers are points in board coordinates, measured in millimeters with +X right and +Y up. For `rotated_rect` pads, undo the emitted counterclockwise rotation about the pad’s center using `rotateDEG` and `applyToPoint` from the existing `transformation-matrix` dependency, then apply the rectangular width/height check. This corrects containment for arbitrary rotations and preserves the existing trace-width tolerance. Update the existing INA237 reproduction and annotated snapshot to expect correct ALERT/SDA/SCL associations. Full-board verification with the original footprint string and the board placement corrections from [sparkfun-boards #361](https://github.com/tscircuit/sparkfun-boards/pull/361): the old core produces 50 traces and 29 vias with seven trace-continuity errors; this fix produces the same copper geometry with zero circuit errors and correct sensor pin/net associations. The untouched original board still skips autorouting because U2 overlaps R4 and its courtyard overlaps R2; those placement corrections are required separately. Validation: - 56 existing related routing tests pass (239 assertions), including the INA237 reproduction and opposite-layer attribution coverage. - The updated INA237 reproduction fails against the pre-fix implementation. - Biome and `git diff --check` pass. - Full TypeScript check attempted: restricted dependency downloads required local source checkouts, which report errors in dependency sources and existing schematic consumers. No diagnostics reference the changed files. Dependency declarations are unchanged.

title: repro: KiCad exports omit hierarchical child schematic files
description: Fixes the issue where KiCad exports do not include hierarchical child schematic files, resulting in blank pages when attempting to open them.
body: ## Motivation Multi-sheet tscircuit designs export a KiCad root schematic that correctly names and references every child sheet, but the CLI writes only that root `.kicad_sch` file. The referenced child schematic files are missing from both the KiCad ZIP and the generated project directory. KiCad therefore shows the expected sheet names in the hierarchy panel, while opening a child sheet produces a blank, unsaved page because its `Sheetfile` cannot be found. This makes an existing schematic look empty and prevents users from reviewing or editing the exported sheets. ## Issue ## Reproduction The fixture declares `power` and `control` schematic sheets and assigns one component to each. The CLI integration tests cover both affected paths: - `tsci export index.tsx -f kicad_zip` - `tsci build index.tsx --kicad-project` In both outputs, the root schematic references `power.kicad_sch` and `control.kicad_sch`, but neither child file is written. The converter already exposes the complete hierarchy through `getOutputFiles()`; the CLI paths currently use only `getOutputString()`, which returns the root file.

title: fix: use native instance references for custom symbols (#640)

Remove that label from the shared drawing and display the placed symbol's native Reference field at the label's position, preserving its font size, alignment, and rotation. Both instances retain the same library ID. Updating an instance's reference updates the visible label.

This change is scoped to the whole-label reference case in #640. It changes only the converter; Circuit JSON and core are unchanged.

The seven updated generated-system SVG snapshots were visually reviewed. Repeated connector labels now read J1/J2/J3/J4 correctly; the remaining visible changes are the native Reference-field colour and alignment. No wiring, symbol geometry, or new label overlaps were found in those changes.

title: Add ti generate-sysconfig-url for hosted viewer links
description: Adds ti generate-sysconfig-url command to generate a URL for hosted read-only viewer links from a .syscfg file without requiring private viewer installation or TI tools.
body:
Adds `ti generate-sysconfig-url ./index.syscfg`, which prints a complete link for the hosted read-only viewer. It preserves the existing filename/source and supports `--viewer-url`; its default is https://sysconfig-viewer.vercel.app/.

The command uses the public `sysconfigts/url` codec, pinned to `e538c5dabfbb1f3d93830c7e3f7d0cc2ff2a5439` from https://github.com/tscircuit/sysconfigts/pull/3. The npm build bundles the encoder, so installed CLI users need no GitHub access, private viewer package, TI tools or SDK for URL generation. `generate-sysconfig-site` remains available separately. Automatic CLI/RunFrame tab wiring stays outside this change.

Rejects invalid input files, invalid UTF-8, oversized source and unsafe viewer addresses. Source is never executed or uploaded. Anyone with the complete URL can decode the source; encoding does not validate the target or pins.

Validation: 70 CLI tests, typecheck, formatting, npm build and the complete npm consumer check passed with the matching local codec contents. After replacing local development aliases with the actual public commit, focused URL tests and formatting pass. GitHub CI also passed formatting and the complete npm package check with the pinned public dependency, including clean installation and bundled CLI consumers. No temporary dependency aliases or private assets are committed.

Shared codec PR #3 is merged. This consumer now pins that merged main commit; its file tree is identical to the tested codec revision. No release or deployment is included.

title: Add native C firmware with PIO step generation
description: DRV8825 controllers currently generate STEP edges in MicroPython, so higher requested speeds can exceed the interpreters pulse throughput. Add a native Pico SDK C application that generates pulses in PIO and counts emitted edges with a separate PIO state machine and DMA. The application retains protocol 3, the existing dashboardgantry commands, 400 ms ramps, deferred GOTO starts, RGBUSB-PD controls, alarms, songs, and temperaturedriverheartbeatwatchdog protections. Native settings use two reserved flash sectors with checksum and partial-write recovery. A build fingerprint identifies the image on live boards. The legacy DRV8847 MicroPython implementation remains available; this native image targets the DRV8825RGB PCB. Validation: Cross-built the UF2 with Pico SDK 2.3.1; native motion, protocolprotection, and settings tests passed with UBSan. Existing 45 Python tests and dashboard, song, single-motor, gantry, and saved-position checks passed. Flashed both physical controllers and checked their build fingerprints. Driver-disabled electrical tests emitted exact requested counts at 1k, 64k, 128k, and 200k physical pulsessec with zero PIO queue underruns. At the 200k setting, observed throughput was approximately 199.7k pulsessec on both boards. Verified heartbeat expiry and USB disconnect stop pulse generation, heartbeats do not resume it, settings survive restart, and restarts return to disabled 5 V with fresh position sessions. No shaft movement or loaded mechanical performance was tested. Independent pulse-widthjitter measurement, loaded torque, and physical positional accuracy remain unverified. CI adds host native tests and an ARM UF2 build.
body:
DRV8825 controllers currently generate STEP edges in MicroPython, so higher requested speeds can exceed the interpreter's pulse throughput. Add a native Pico SDK C application that generates pulses in PIO and counts emitted edges with a separate PIO state machine and DMA.

The application retains protocol 3, the existing dashboard/gantry commands, 400 ms ramps, deferred GOTO starts, RGB/USB-PD controls, alarms, songs, and temperature/driver/heartbeat/watchdog protections. Native settings use two reserved flash sectors with checksum and partial-write recovery. A build fingerprint identifies the image on live boards. The legacy DRV8847 MicroPython implementation remains available; this native image targets the DRV8825/RGB PCB.

Validation:
- Cross-built the UF2 with Pico SDK 2.3.1; native motion, protocol/protection, and settings tests passed with UBSan.
- Existing 45 Python tests and dashboard, song, single-motor, gantry, and saved-position checks passed.
- Flashed both physical controllers and checked their build fingerprints. Driver-disabled electrical tests emitted exact requested counts at 1k, 64k, 128k, and 200k physical pulses/sec with zero PIO queue underruns. At the 200k setting, observed throughput was approximately 199.7k pulses/sec on both boards.
- Verified heartbeat expiry and USB disconnect stop pulse generation, heartbeats do not resume it, settings survive restart, and restarts return to disabled 5 V with fresh position sessions.

No shaft movement or loaded mechanical performance was tested. Independent pulse-width/jitter measurement, loaded torque, and physical positional accuracy remain unverified. CI adds host native tests and an ARM UF2 build.

title: Add macOS terminal installation without browser quarantine
description: Add a macOS terminal installer that downloads a specified release with curl, selects arm64 or x64 automatically, verifies the selected archive against SHA256SUMS before extracting, and preserves all redistribution notices.
body:
Browser-downloaded macOS releases inherit quarantine metadata from the browser and can be blocked by Gatekeeper despite having a valid ad hoc signature. The metadata is added on the user's Mac, so removing attributes during release packaging cannot prevent this behavior.

Add a macOS terminal installer that downloads a specified release with curl, selects arm64 or x64 automatically, verifies the selected archive against SHA256SUMS before extracting, and preserves all redistribution notices. Existing destinations are refused, and temporary downloads are cleaned up. This provides an installation path that does not acquire browser quarantine and requires no Apple account, sudo, or Bun/Node installation.

Document the installer in the README and include a source-commit-pinned command in daily/manual release notes. Document the file-specific quarantine workaround for existing browser downloads. Browser downloads remain subject to Gatekeeper; this change does not claim to make them notarized or disable macOS security settings.

Validation:
- `bun test tests/install-macos.test.ts tests/daily-release.test.ts` — 26 passed, including both architectures, checksum rejection, download failures, and preservation of existing installations.
- `sh -n scripts/install-macos.sh` and `git diff --check` passed.
